**Section III: Comprehension (10 marks)**

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions below in your own words. You are strongly advised to read the entire text before you start answering the questions.

**To own a gun or not to own a gun?**

Canadians have long prided themselves on living in a law-abiding society where violence is not a constant threat. Now they wonder. A series of fatal shootings over recent years has aroused fears that Canada may be going America's way, not least America's ways with guns.

A coalition for Gun Control, backed by police, legal, educational, health, local government and women's groups, has campaigned strongly for tighter controls. But Canada has its own gun lobby. Over the past couple of months, the National Firearms Association (NFA) has united hunters, target shooters and collectors in protest rallies. A demonstration by 5,000 outside parliament in Ottawa told the Minister of Justice to 'target criminals, not gun-owners'. The gun lobby has bombarded rural members of parliament with letters, faxes and threats of ballot revenge.

Laws were strengthened after the massacre of 14 women students at the University of Montreal by a gunman with an assault rifle in 1989. New types of weapons were restricted or prohibited, new requirements added for obtaining a gun permit. But the political opposition prevented the Conservative government of the day from going as far as many Canadians wanted. Since then, further murders and random shootings of policemen, shopkeepers, even a youth in a parking-lot dispute, have kept concern at high pitch.

Already, all would-be owners must be scrutinised and take a safety course. Deadly automatic weapons are prohibited. Ownership of handguns and semi-automatic weapons is subject to tight restriction and registration. Ordinary rifles and shotguns are not subject to registration, but all firearms must be stored safely. Even so, Canadians own around 6 million guns, about 1 million of them handguns.

Mr Rock is convinced that guns will be used less in crime if they are less available. His reforms, as he has outlined them, may include: tougher measures on gun smuggling, tougher penalties for illegal possession of guns and for their use in crimes; new strict controls on the sale of ammunition, prohibition of replicas; tighter restrictions, even possibly a complete ban, on handguns and semi-automatic weapons.

What the gun lobby is against is the requirement to register guns. Many people in rural areas own rifles and shotguns for hunting, to protect themselves at times against bears. There is need for tougher crime controls, not gun control, say the protesters. They argue that registration would be ineffective, costly and a bureaucratic intrusion into their freedom. They further argue that they have a 'right to bear arms' and need them for self-defence against criminals.

Statistics challenge the public belief that gun-related crime is out of control. Guns are responsible for 32% of homicides, as they have been in each year of the past decade. Canada had 193 such cases last year, about one-sixth as many, relative to population, as the United States. Robbery with firearms consistently averages about 27% of all robberies. There has been a nasty rise in the use of handguns, however.

Whatever the figures, most Canadians strongly favour tougher controls. A poll a year ago found 86% for a ban on assault weapons, and 71% who would ban all handguns too. Yet Mr Rock faces a tough fight to get his reforms through. Parliamentarians from rural constituencies, in particular, support the gun lobby.

*(Culled from The Economist, October 29th - November 4th 1994)*

**Questions**

1. What does the author mean by "America's way" in paragraph one? (2 marks)

2. What two groups confront each other in the argument over gun control? (1 mark)

3. How can the gun lobby carry out the "ballot revenge"? (2 marks)

4. List 2 new measures to be taken to combat crime by Mr Rock. (1 mark)

5. Do you think it is the right of every citizen who feels like owning a gun to have one? Justify your reason. (2 marks)

6. Are Canadians justified in thinking that their society is becoming more and more violent? Justify your answer. (2 marks)

**Question concernée : n°1 (2 marks).**

### Rappel de méthode
Une question de compréhension se répond en reformulant un passage précis du texte, avec ses propres mots autant que possible. Sur un texte argumentatif comme celui-ci, il faut distinguer clairement les faits chiffrés (statistiques citées) des positions défendues par chaque camp (le lobby des armes contre la coalition pour le contrôle des armes), pour ne pas confondre une opinion rapportée avec un fait établi par le texte.

Par « America's way », l'auteur désigne le mode de vie américain caractérisé par une large diffusion des armes à feu dans la population et une culture de la violence armée qui en découle. Les Canadiens craignent que leur propre société, longtemps considérée comme respectueuse des lois et peu violente, ne commence à ressembler à celle des États-Unis sur ce plan précis, après une série de fusillades meurtrières récentes.

Un encadrement (formation à la sécurité, enregistrement, restrictions selon le type d'arme) me semble un compromis plus raisonnable qu'un droit inconditionnel.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Les statistiques citées dans le texte nuancent cette impression : la part des homicides liés aux armes à feu (32%) et celle des vols à main armée (27%) sont restées stables sur toute la dernière décennie, ce qui ne traduit pas une explosion soudaine de la violence. Le texte signale cependant une hausse préoccupante de l'usage des armes de poing en particulier, ce qui justifie une inquiétude ciblée sur ce point précis, sans pour autant valider l'idée d'une société globalement de plus en plus violente dans son ensemble.

### Piège à éviter
Cette question invite à croiser des statistiques stables avec une inquiétude ponctuelle réelle (la hausse des armes de poing) : répondre simplement « oui » ou « non » sans mobiliser les chiffres du texte prive la réponse de sa justification attendue.

### Conseil
Quand un texte argumentatif fournit des statistiques précises, utilise-les systématiquement pour appuyer ta réponse plutôt que de te contenter d'une impression générale tirée du ton du texte : c'est ce qui distingue une réponse bien justifiée d'une simple opinion.

incertitudes: Questions 5 et 6 appellent une réponse personnelle argumentée : les propositions fournies sont des exemples de réponses recevables parmi d'autres, non l'unique corrigé officiel.

Quelques mots du texte source, numérisé puis reconverti, présentaient des déformations évidentes ('nutter' pour 'gunman', 'bas' pour 'has', 'bandguns' pour 'handguns', 'flot' pour d'autres occurrences dans le même corpus) ; ils ont été silencieusement corrigés pour la reproduction du texte.
